title: Functorial tangent action on marked lifts
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and use $\mathrm{Art}_k=\mathcal C_{k,k}$ and the notions of predeformation category and (RS) from [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Let $\mathcal F$ be a groupoid-valued pseudofunctor on $\mathrm{Art}_k$ with $\mathcal F(k)$ equivalent to the groupoid with one object and one arrow. Assume that $\mathcal F$ satisfies (RS): for $A_1\to A\leftarrow A_2$ with $A_2\to A$ surjective, the canonical functor to the groupoid of pairs equipped with an isomorphism over $A$ is an equivalence
$$\mathcal F(A_1\times_A A_2)\simeq\mathcal F(A_1)\times_{\mathcal F(A)}\mathcal F(A_2).$$
Put $T\mathcal F=\pi_0\mathcal F(k[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2))$ with its canonical deformation $k$-vector structure [lem-sfb-artin-rs-tangent-tensor]. Let $A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ be a surjection in $\mathrm{Art}_k$ with kernel $I$ annihilated by $\mathfrak m_{A'}$, and let $x\in\mathcal F(A)$. Define $\operatorname{Lift}_{\mathcal F}(x,A')$ as the set of isomorphism classes of pairs $(x',\alpha)$ with $x'\in\mathcal F(A')$ and $\alpha:x'|_A\xrightarrow{\sim}x$; an isomorphism $u:(x',\alpha)\to(x'',\alpha'')$ must satisfy $\alpha''\circ u|_A=\alpha$. If this set is nonempty, it has a canonical action of the additive group $T\mathcal F\otimes_k I$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] which is free and transitive: for any $z,w$ in it there is a unique $t$ with $w=z+t$. If $H:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ is a morphism commuting coherently with base change and $\mathcal G$ satisfies the same hypotheses, the induced map on marked lift classes obeys
$$H(z+t)=H(z)+(dH\otimes1_I)(t),$$
where $dH:T\mathcal F\to T\mathcal G$ is the map on isomorphism classes over the dual numbers.

source.place: Tag 06JI (lemma-free-transitive-action) and Tag 06JJ (remark-free-transitive-action-functorial); marked lift classes are those of definition-lifts.

proof.text: Write $L=L_{\mathcal F}(x,A')$ and $x_0=x|_k$. The marking definition agrees with $L_{\mathcal F}$ in [lem-sfb-rs-marked-lift-pullback-bijections]. Put $k[I]=k\oplus I$ with the multiplication of [def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category]. Since $I\subset\mathfrak m_{A'}$, we have $I^2=0$. Every $k$-subspace of $I$ is an $A'$-ideal, since multiplication by $a$ acts on $I$ as its residue $\bar a$. Thus $I$ is finite-dimensional: otherwise the spans of successive tails of a countably infinite independent sequence give a strictly descending chain of ideals of $A'$. All fibre rings below belong to $\mathrm{Art}_k$: projection onto $A'$ has square-zero kernel a finite direct sum of $I$, with residue field $k$. For a descending ideal chain, its images in $A'$ and its intersections with this kernel stabilize, and then the chain itself stabilizes by subtraction of representatives. The nonunits are exactly the elements whose common residue is zero. As $\mathcal F(k)$ is contractible, forgetting the unique marking to $x_0$ identifies $L_{\mathcal F}(x_0,k[I])$ canonically with $\pi_0\mathcal F(k[I])$. Apply [lem-sfb-artin-rs-tangent-tensor] with $R=k$ and $V=I$ to identify this set with $M=T\mathcal F\otimes_k I$.

Let $B=A'\times_A A'$ and $C=A'\times_k k[I]$. Define $g:B\to k[I]$ by $g(a,b)=(\bar a,b-a)$. To check multiplicativity, write $b=a+i$ and $d=c+j$; then $bd-ac=aj+ci+ij=\bar a j+\bar c i$, since $ij=0$. Hence
$$s:B\xrightarrow{\sim}C,\qquad (a,b)\mapsto(a,(\bar a,b-a))$$
is a local $k$-algebra isomorphism, with inverse $(a,(\bar a,i))\mapsto(a,a+i)$. Both $s$ and its inverse commute with first projection to $A'$. For a representative $(z,\alpha)$ of a class in $L$, apply the fixed-lift bijection of [lem-sfb-rs-marked-lift-pullback-bijections] to $A'\to A\leftarrow A'$ with fixed lift $(z,\alpha)$, obtaining $L_{\mathcal F}(z,B)\cong L$. Apply it also to $A'\to k\leftarrow k[I]$ with fixed lift $z\to x_0$, obtaining $L_{\mathcal F}(z,C)\cong L_{\mathcal F}(x_0,k[I])$. Transport by $s$ identifies the middle marked lift sets. Their composite is a bijection $\delta_z:L\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. Concretely $\delta_z(w)$ is transport along $g$ of the (RS) gluing of $z,w$ with their markings to $x$. These comparisons are independent of representatives by the naturality in marked isomorphisms in the cited node.

source.place: Tag 06JI, equations (one), (two), (three) and the first-factor-preserving bijection.

proof.text:
For $z,w,v\in L$, glue them over $x$ to an object over $E=A'\times_A A'\times_A A'$ using the first bijection of [lem-sfb-rs-marked-lift-pullback-bijections] twice. The projection $A'\times_A A'\to A$ is surjective, so both applications satisfy its hypotheses. Projection to a pair recovers the marked gluing used to define $\delta$ by naturality. There are ring maps
$$h:E\to k[I\oplus I],\quad(a,b,c)\mapsto(\bar a,b-a,c-b),\qquad \sigma:k[I\oplus I]\to k[I],\quad(r,i,j)\mapsto(r,i+j).$$
Here $k[I\oplus I]=k[I]\times_k k[I]$. Its two projections composed with $h$ are $g_{12}$ and $g_{23}$, and $\sigma h=g_{13}$ because $(b-a)+(c-b)=c-a$. Consequently the transported class over $k[I\oplus I]$ has components $\delta_z(w),\delta_w(v)$; [lem-sfb-artin-rs-tangent-tensor], applied to the two coordinate projections and to the linear sum $I\oplus I\to I$, sends it to their sum. Thus
$$\delta_z(v)=\delta_z(w)+\delta_w(v).$$

The cocycle identity with $z=w=v$ gives $\delta_z(z)=0$ by cancellation in $M$. Define $z+t$ to be the unique $w$ with $\delta_z(w)=t$, using the bijectivity from step 2. Then $z+0=z$. If $w=z+t$ and $v=w+u$, the cocycle identity gives $\delta_z(v)=t+u$, hence $(z+t)+u=z+(t+u)$. This is an additive group action. For fixed $z,w$, its unique translation parameter is $\delta_z(w)$, so the action is free and transitive. No initial element of $L$ has been chosen for its definition: the same rule defines it simultaneously for every $z$.

source.place: Tag 06JI, definition of the action and its final sentence.

proof.text:
Let $H:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be as in the statement. Naturality in the pseudofunctor of [lem-sfb-rs-marked-lift-pullback-bijections] makes the marked gluing and fixed-lift comparisons commute with $H$, and coherent commutation with transport makes the maps induced by $s,g$ commute on isomorphism classes. The induced map on the square-zero classes is $dH\otimes1_I$: to check this, choose a basis of the finite-dimensional space $I$ and use its coordinate maps $k[I]\to k[\epsilon]$. By [lem-sfb-artin-rs-tangent-tensor] these detect the tensor coordinates, and in each coordinate the map is exactly $dH$ by definition. Moreover $dH$ is $k$-linear: scalar maps $(a,v)\mapsto(a,cv)$ and the sum map $k[k\oplus k]\to k[k]$ define the canonical scalar and addition operations; $H$ commutes with these maps and with both projections. Thus
$$\delta^{\mathcal G}_{H(z)}(H(w))=(dH\otimes1_I)(\delta^{\mathcal F}_z(w)).$$
Set $w=z+t$ and use the unique-parameter rule of step 4 in $\mathcal G$ to obtain $H(z+t)=H(z)+(dH\otimes1_I)(t)$.

lean.statement: theorem deformation_marked_lift_torsor (F : CofibredGroupoids.{u, v, w} k k) (G : CofibredGroupoids.{u, v', w'} k k) (hpreF : IsPredeformation F) (hrsF : IsRimSchlessinger F) (hpreG : IsPredeformation G) (hrsG : IsRimSchlessinger G) {A B : TestCategory k k} (p : B ⟶ A) (hs : Function.Surjective (map p)) (hk : ∀ b ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal (ring B), ∀ i ∈ RingHom.ker (map p).toRingHom, b * i = 0) : ∃ (_ : MarkedLiftTangentData F) (_ : MarkedLiftTangentData G) (_ : FiniteDimensional k (liftKernel p)) (actF : ∀ x : fibre F A, AddAction (TensorProduct k (tangentSet F) (liftKernel p)) (markedLiftClasses F p x)) (actG : ∀ x : fibre G A, AddAction (TensorProduct k (tangentSet G) (liftKernel p)) (markedLiftClasses G p x)), (∀ x : fibre F A, IsCanonicalMarkedLiftAction F p hs x (actF x)) ∧ (∀ x : fibre G A, IsCanonicalMarkedLiftAction G p hs x (actG x)) ∧ (∀ (x : fibre F A) (z w : markedLiftClasses F p x), ∃! t, (actF x).vadd t z = w) ∧ (∀ (x : fibre G A) (z w : markedLiftClasses G p x), ∃! t, (actG x).vadd t z = w) ∧ (∀ H : DeformationMorphism F G, ∃ dH : tangentSet F →ₗ[k] tangentSet G, (∀ t, dH t = deformationTangentMap H t) ∧ ∀ (x : fibre F A) (z : markedLiftClasses F p x) (t : TensorProduct k (tangentSet F) (liftKernel p)), markedLiftMorphism H p x ((actF x).vadd t z) = (actG ((H.app A).obj x)).vadd (TensorProduct.map dH (LinearMap.id : liftKernel p →ₗ[k] liftKernel p) t) (markedLiftMorphism H p x z))
lean.note: Marked lifts are actual costructured arrows for the recorded push functor. The theorem supplies normalized tangent tensor data, proves finite-dimensionality of the actual kernel, and supplies the canonical actions simultaneously for F and G and every x, with unique translations and equivariance for every coherent morphism. The canonical-action predicate pins the algebra map pointwise to (residue(a), b-a) and identifies translation with its transport of the RS gluing. Empty lift sets carry the unique empty action; freeness and transitivity are expressed by unique parameters for every pair. The componentwise morphism interface retains independent source and target fibre universes.
